lead: On the memory of Sts Cyril and Methodius, apostles of the Slav peoples, the Epistle praises God's plan to gather up all things in Christ, and the Gospel shows Jesus praying all night before he chooses the Twelve. God's plan reaches every people through those whom Christ sends. The key words are gather up, seal and apostles.

r.h: To gather up all things in Christ
set: In the Greek, Ephesians 1:3–14 is one long sentence of blessing, praising the Father who chose us, the Son in whom we are redeemed, and the Spirit with whom we are sealed. Today's verses are its second half. On Sunday we heard the prayer that follows this hymn (1:15–23).
str: vv. 7–10: redemption and forgiveness; the mystery of God's will: to gather up all things in Christ.
vv. 11–12: we who first hoped in Christ have an inheritance.
vv. 13–14: you also, hearing and believing, were sealed with the Spirit, the pledge of our inheritance.
kw: Literally, to sum up under one head (kephalē). All things, in heaven and on earth, scattered by sin, are to be brought together in Christ. St Irenaeus built his teaching of “recapitulation” on this word.
A seal marked ownership and protected what was sealed. The baptized are marked as God's own by the Holy Spirit.
A down payment, the first part of a price that guarantees the rest. The Spirit is God's first gift and the promise of all that is to come.
vv: In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses,
Redemption is the language of setting slaves at liberty. It is paid, Paul says, not in silver but in the blood of Christ.
to gather up all things in him, things in heaven and things on earth.
God's plan is not to save a few souls out of a ruined world, but to bring the whole creation into unity in Christ.
were marked with the seal of the promised Holy Spirit;
Hearing, believing, being sealed: the path of every Christian, from the word preached to the sacraments received.
ch: The Catechism teaches that Confirmation, like Baptism, marks the Christian with an indelible seal, the sign that he belongs totally to Christ, and it cites this passage (CCC 1295–1296). St Irenaeus taught that Christ “recapitulated” in himself the whole history of humanity, undoing Adam's disobedience by his obedience (in substance). Cyril and Methodius gave the Slav peoples the Scriptures and the liturgy in their own tongue, so that they too could hear “the word of truth” and be gathered into Christ.

r.h: He spent the night in prayer and chose the Twelve
set: Opposition to Jesus is growing. After he healed a man's withered hand on the sabbath, his opponents “were filled with fury and discussed with one another what they might do to Jesus” (6:11). At this moment Jesus goes up the mountain to pray. Luke shows Jesus praying before every great moment: at his baptism (3:21), before Peter's confession (9:18), at the Transfiguration (9:28–29) and on the Mount of Olives (22:41).
str: v. 12: a night of prayer on the mountain.
v. 13: at daybreak he chooses twelve and names them apostles.
vv. 14–16: the names, from Simon Peter to Judas Iscariot.
kw: A word used only here in the New Testament. The choice of the Twelve is born of a whole night with the Father.
One who is sent, an envoy. Twelve recalls the twelve tribes of Israel: Jesus is gathering and renewing God's people.
vv: he spent the night in prayer to God.
Before he acts, Jesus prays. The Church still prays before choosing her ministers, as she did before the choice of Matthias (Acts 1:24).
chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles:
From a larger group of disciples Jesus chooses some for a special mission. Today's saints, Cyril and Methodius, are called “apostles of the Slavs” because they continued that mission.
and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
Luke does not hide it. Judas too was chosen after a night of prayer. God's call is real, and so is human freedom.
ch: The Catechism notes that Jesus prays before the decisive moments of his mission, including the choice of the Twelve (CCC 2600). It teaches that Jesus chose the Twelve with Peter as their head and that they are the foundation stones of the Church (CCC 765), and that the apostles' mission continues in the bishops, their successors (CCC 860–862).

qa: Why did Jesus choose Judas, if he knew he would betray him?

The Gospels do not answer every question. They show that Jesus' choice was real and his love sincere, and that Judas chose to turn away. Even the betrayal could not defeat God's plan; God brought salvation out of it.
rite: Sts Cyril and Methodius were brothers from Thessalonica in the ninth century. They went as missionaries to the Slav peoples of Moravia, created an alphabet for their language, and translated the Scriptures and the liturgy into Slavonic. Pope Adrian II approved their Slavonic liturgy in Rome. St John Paul II named them co-patrons of Europe (1980) and wrote of them in the encyclical Slavorum Apostoli (1985). The Byzantine Churches honour them today, and the Latin Church on 14 February. Our own Church knows the gift they gave: we pray the Holy Qurbono of the ancient Antiochene tradition in Malayalam, while keeping the treasures of Syriac.
study: Paul says the Spirit is the pledge of our inheritance. How do I live as one who has already received God's first gift?
Jesus prayed all night before an important choice. What decision in my life should I bring to prayer before I act?
